result.title: Reliable Risk Estimation with Kernel Mean Matching under Dependent Sampling
result.summary: Kernel Mean Matching (KMM) estimates risk under covariate shift by reweighting labelled source samples so that their kernel mean embedding matches that of unlabeled target samples. Existing finite-sample guarantees are usually stated for independent samples, although many applications involve temporal, spatial, or clustered dependence. We give a finite-sample KMM analysis under dependent sampling by replacing nominal sample sizes with effective sample sizes in the concentration steps used by the classical proof. The approach uses Bernstein inequalities for geometrically strongly mixing processes and derives a model-based effective sample size. The resulting bound separates overlap, dependence, and smoothness effects with specific constants derived under a Gaussian process assumption. This analysis yields an additional tradeoff: smoother losses preserve more input dependence and therefore reduce effective sample size, while also reducing function complexity and empirical-to-population risk gaps. Applying the result to prediction yields confidence intervals that achieve near-nominal coverage in synthetic experiments and substantially reduce undercoverage on real monitoring data.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究依赖采样（几何强混合过程）下核均值匹配（KMM）的有限样本风险估计，用基于高斯过程假设的有效样本量替换经典证明中的名义样本量，得到分离重叠、依赖性与损失平滑度影响的界，并在合成实验与真实监控数据上给出覆盖率更好的预测置信区间。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关联，但其依赖采样下的有效样本量刻画及「更平滑损失保留更多依赖、降低有效样本量」的权衡，可能可供核查地借用于评估共享前缀或时序相关的多条推理轨迹与 latent 状态统计；迁移属推测。
